## What did you do? (clear steps if possible)

We are embedding a (slightly modified) version of the F-Droid Client into our AOSP16 ROM and send the `org.fdroid.action.UPDATE_REPOS` broadcast-intent from the `com.android.provision` app upon completing of the device provisioning.

The F-Droid client is installed as a privileged app and receives `android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS` through `default-permissions.xml` and `android.permission.INSTALL_PACKAGES` through `privapp-permission.xml` 

The `com.android.provision` app is more or less the AOSP default one, but extending the `finishSetup()` function by the broadcast intent:

```
        Intent intent = new Intent("org.fdroid.action.UPDATE_REPOS");
        ComponentName componentName = new ComponentName(
                "eu.pretix.marketplace.client.android.basic",
                "org.fdroid.fdroid.receiver.RepoUpdateReceiver"
        );
        intent.setComponent(componentName);
        sendBroadcast(intent);
```

The client is shipping with a modified `default_repos.xml` 

## What did you expect to see?

I would expect the F-Droid client to receive the Broadcast Intent in the `RepoUpdateReceiver`, run the `RepoUpdateWorker.updateNow()`, download the repo index and install any available updates.

## What did you see instead?

The Intent is received and some work is being done. However, `RepoUpdateManager.updateRepos()` seems to be called a second time and being dismissed (`Not updating, only 488 ms since last check`).

## Further observations

It seems like this second call is however where the magic would have happened - removing the `MIN_UPDATE_INTERVAL_MILLIS`-check will indeed retrieve the repository index and install any available updates.

As a work-around we have disabled the check in our client and things seem to be working fine now.

As a curiosity: On our AOSP 13 ROM, this is not happening - there the installation just works. I thin this _might_ perhaps be related to changes to Android's foreground services.

For debugging purposes, I removed the `protectionLevel` of the `UPDATE_REPOS`-permission and issued update-commands through adb (`adb shell am broadcast -a org.fdroid.action.UPDATE_REPOS -n eu.pretix.marketplace.client.android.basic.debug/org.fdroid.fdroid.receiver.RepoUpdateReceiver`) - starting with a fresh install of the F-Droid Client apk, making sure it was not running after installation.

Source of our modified client: https://github.com/pretix/marketplace-client-android

Changes from stock F-Droid Basic Client:

* Name/Logo
* default repos
* default settings (disabling Tor)
* "update at Night"-feature
  * Adding a `updateAtNight`-tag to `PeriodicWorkRequestBuilder`
  * Adding linear 2 hour Backoff-Criteria to `PeriodicWorkRequestBuilder`
  * Postponing/retrying work that is tagged `updateAtNight` if executed outside of 2..\<6 o'clock
* Removed the `MIN_UPDATE_INTERVAL_MILLIS` check (workaround for this issue)

I am fairly confident, that the `updateAtNight`-feature in our fork is not responsible for this issue, since we have observed this problem even before we merged it.
